decisions.summary: The push's in-progress refusal keeps its old open-box test ('^\s*- \[ \]', any indentation) and exempts only a spec whose status line begins with a closing word (Done / Superseded by / Withdrawn), asked of speckit-todo.py --closed-by-status; error or empty answer = not closed.
decisions.why: Narrows a standing guard, but the accepted spec requires it: FR-004 closes features by their status line and D3 leaves their tasks unticked, so the literal old rule would refuse every FR-004 closure as in-progress work and defeat the request's purpose (one true, mechanical state). Round 5 confirmed the exemption is now ONLY this: the grep line is byte-identical to the pre-feature guard (git show 8b93f015b~1:scripts/sync-with-main.sh), and the exemption fails closed (output must equal 'yes').

decisions.summary: Round 4's finding: the refusal's box reader switched to column-0 tasks and 'filed' went unrefused. Round 5: the refusal reads boxes exactly as before (any '^\s*- \[ \]'); speckit-todo's state/box parser no longer decides the guard.
decisions.why: Fixed as asked. Verified 2026-10-08 by running tests/hooks/test-sync-with-main.sh in the clone (108 checks pass), including 'indented open tasks -> refused' and 'a ticked task with an open indented research box -> refused' (both would land under round 4's --state code: they parse as filed / closed), plus the Done-lands and Implemented-refused cases; make test-file tests/tooling/test_speckit_todo.py 24 passed, including the parametrized --closed-by-status test. No box reading is narrowed any more.

decisions.summary: review-gate.sh exempts from the fidelity-verdict check a spec whose status opens 'Filed' and whose directory has no tasks.md; gaining tasks.md ends the exemption.
decisions.why: Implied by the request: the GM asked that future-work entries 'become an unimplemented spec kit feature', and FR-006/FR-008 make filing (verbatim text, status Filed, no plan or tasks) the routine way to defer work. A filed spec implements nothing, and constitution XVI's review is before implementation; without the exemption every deferral needs an escape. The exemption is narrow: it keys on both the Filed status AND no tasks.md, ends when tasks appear (tested both ways), and opens nothing the gate held, since code pushed without touching the spec directory was never under this check. Round 5: plan bytes outside D8 unchanged (HEAD~1 plan.md hashes to round 4's e533c6ca...; 6 changed lines, all in D8).
